title: Add safe capture sessions and controls

fields.outcome: Documentation captures can switch user sessions safely and prevent sensitive values or unintended admin changes from appearing in capture output.
fields.scope: Support per-module session selection (such as signed-out, end-user, and administrator), a built-in sign-out action, secret guards, value masking that preserves useful empty-secret-field visuals, and a read-only mode that blocks non-GET requests for designated captures. Define safe storage and reporting of session credentials.
fields.acceptance: Modules can select named session setup without storing credentials in committed specs. Sign-out is available as a supported action. Secret guards stop or redact configured secrets. Value masking hides populated sensitive values while preserving intended empty-field visuals. Read-only mode blocks non-GET requests and reports blocked attempts.
fields.verification: Use isolated browser fixtures to cover session switching and sign-out, secret appearance in outputs, value masking behavior on populated and empty fields, and blocked non-GET requests under read-only mode.
fields.risks: A browser-level read-only guard may not cover side effects caused by GET endpoints or external systems. Document its boundary and retain isolated test accounts and environments.
fields.source: Consumer feedback supplied by the user on 2026-11-03; scope and acceptance remain discovery-stage proposals.

criteria.expectation: Each module can select an explicitly configured signed-out, user, or administrator session without embedding credentials in tracked files.
The journey supports a built-in sign-out operation that clears the selected authenticated session as configured.
Configured secret guards prevent protected values from being emitted into screenshots, reports, or generated documentation.
Sensitive populated values can be masked while empty secret fields remain visible when useful for instructions.
Read-only mode blocks non-GET requests during designated captures and records blocked attempts.
